# Image specification

**Generated from `src/lib/image-slots.ts`. Do not edit this file — edit the
registry and run `pnpm docs:images`.**

This is what to upload, and what the site does with it.

## The short version

Upload the biggest, uncropped version you have. The site handles the rest: it
crops each photograph for every place it appears, generates the smaller sizes,
converts the format, and holds on to the subject rather than the middle of the
frame when something has to be cut. You do not need to prepare a different file
per section, and you should not try to.

## Sizes at a glance

| Where it appears | Shape it renders at | Minimum | Upload this | Slot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Homepage hero** | Any. Cropped to fill the window, so it must work wide and tall. | 2560px wide | 3200px wide, any height | `heroSlide` |
| **Departure page header** | Any. Cropped to fill a 74vh band. | 2400px wide | 3000px wide, any height | `departureHero` |
| **Departure card** | 4:3 landscape | 1200 × 900 px | 1600 × 1200 px | `departureCard` |
| **Gallery, full size** | Any. Shown complete, letterboxed against a dark ground. | 2048px wide | 2560px wide, any height | `galleryLightbox` |
| **Gallery thumbnail** | 3:2 landscape | 240 × 160 px | 320 × 213 px | `galleryThumb` |
| **Guide portrait** | 4:5 portrait | 800 × 1000 px | 1200 × 1500 px | `guidePortrait` |
| **Journal cover** | 16:9 landscape | 1800 × 1013 px | 2400 × 1350 px | `journalCover` |
| **Region card** | 3:4 portrait | 900 × 1200 px | 1200 × 1600 px | `regionCard` |

Every figure is a **minimum**, not a target. The site never upscales — a file
below the minimum is soft on a retina screen, and softness reads as cheapness
rather than as a mistake.

## Rules that apply to every upload

**Do not crop before uploading.** Upload the full frame. The site crops for each place the photograph appears, and it will do a better job with the whole picture than with one that has already lost its edges. A photograph cropped for the card will be the wrong shape for the header.

**Upload the largest version you have.** Every size below is a minimum, not a target. The site generates smaller versions automatically and serves the right one for each screen; it cannot invent detail that was not uploaded. A file that is too big costs nothing but upload time. A file that is too small looks cheap on every retina screen, which is most of them.

**JPEG or PNG, sRGB.** The site converts to modern formats itself. Do not upload HEIC from an iPhone without converting first, and do not upload anything in Adobe RGB or ProPhoto — the colours will shift on the web.

**Set a focal point when the subject is off-centre.** The default keeps the middle of the frame, slightly high. If the subject is at one edge, set the focal point when you upload and every crop on the site will hold on to it instead.

**Landscape unless the slot says otherwise.** Two slots are portrait — guide portraits and region cards — and everything else is wide or square. A portrait photograph in a wide slot loses most of its height, which usually means it loses the sky and the ground and keeps a band across the middle.

**Nothing important in the bottom third of a hero.** The homepage hero and the departure header both carry type across their lower portion under a dark scrim. A face or a caption-worthy detail down there will be behind text.

**The caption is the point.** Photographs on this site carry factual captions describing what is in the frame. Upload something that a plain sentence can describe accurately. A photograph that needs an adjective to be worth showing is not worth showing here.

## Each slot in detail

### Homepage hero

The full-bleed photograph behind the headline on the homepage. Seen first, at the largest size anywhere on the site.

- **Shape** — Any. Cropped to fill the window, so it must work wide and tall.
- **Minimum upload** — 2560px wide
- **Upload this** — 3200px wide, any height
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `heroSlide`

> Headline type sits over the lower left. Avoid photographs whose subject is in that corner, and avoid anything with fine detail there — the scrim will flatten it.

### Departure page header

The slider across the top of a departure page. Every gallery photograph for that trek appears here at full width.

- **Shape** — Any. Cropped to fill a 74vh band.
- **Minimum upload** — 2400px wide
- **Upload this** — 3000px wide, any height
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `departureHero`

> The trek name and the spec row sit over the bottom third under a dark scrim. A subject low in the frame will be behind type.

### Departure card

The photograph at the top of each departure card, on the homepage grid and the departures index.

- **Shape** — 4:3 landscape
- **Minimum upload** — 1200 × 900 px
- **Upload this** — 1600 × 1200 px
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `departureCard`

> Rendered at about 410px wide on a desktop and full width on a phone, which is why the minimum is higher than it looks like it needs to be.

### Gallery, full size

The photograph shown when somebody opens one from a slider. Fitted whole, never cropped.

- **Shape** — Any. Shown complete, letterboxed against a dark ground.
- **Minimum upload** — 2048px wide
- **Upload this** — 2560px wide, any height
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `galleryLightbox`

> The only slot that shows the whole frame, so it is the one where a crooked horizon or a cluttered edge is visible.

### Gallery thumbnail

The small strip under a slider used to jump between photographs.

- **Shape** — 3:2 landscape
- **Minimum upload** — 240 × 160 px
- **Upload this** — 320 × 213 px
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `galleryThumb`

> Generated from the same upload as the slide it points at. Nothing is uploaded separately for this.

### Guide portrait

A guide or staff photograph, for the licence and team material. Not yet on a page.

- **Shape** — 4:5 portrait
- **Minimum upload** — 800 × 1000 px
- **Upload this** — 1200 × 1500 px
- **Focal point** — defaults to top
- **Slot name in code** — `guidePortrait`

> Focal point is the top of the frame, so a portrait shot at any ratio keeps the face when it is cropped square.

### Journal cover

The lead photograph on a journal entry. Not yet on a page.

- **Shape** — 16:9 landscape
- **Minimum upload** — 1800 × 1013 px
- **Upload this** — 2400 × 1350 px
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `journalCover`

> Wide and short. A tall upload loses most of its height here, so choose something horizontal if you have the option.

### Region card

A region or activity tile. Not yet on a page.

- **Shape** — 3:4 portrait
- **Minimum upload** — 900 × 1200 px
- **Upload this** — 1200 × 1600 px
- **Focal point** — defaults to center
- **Slot name in code** — `regionCard`

> The only tall slot on the site. A wide upload loses its left and right edges here.

## How the automatic fitting works

Every photograph on the site is rendered through one component,
`<SiteImage slot="…">`, which reads the registry above. That means:

- **Cropped, never squashed.** Images fill their box with `object-cover`, so
  the shape of the box never distorts the picture.
- **The crop keeps the subject.** The focal point sets `object-position`, and
  the default sits slightly above centre because that is where subjects are —
  a centred crop of a person keeps the chin and loses the head.
- **The space is reserved before the file arrives.** The aspect ratio is applied
  by the wrapper, so nothing on the page moves as images load.
- **The browser downloads a file sized for the box.** Each slot carries its own
  `sizes`, so a 96px thumbnail fetches a 96px file and a full-bleed header
  fetches a wide one, from the same upload.

### If a photograph is the wrong shape for a slot

It still works, and here is exactly what happens. A tall photograph in a wide
slot keeps a horizontal band through the focal point and loses the top and
bottom. A wide photograph in a tall slot keeps a vertical band and loses the
sides. Nothing is stretched and nothing is letterboxed, except in the full-size
gallery view, which is the one place the whole frame is shown.

If a particular photograph crops badly, set its focal point rather than
re-cropping the file. That fixes it in every slot at once.

## When the admin upload screen is built

The registry is the contract. An upload form should:

1. Reject anything narrower than the smallest `minWidth` above, with the
   figure in the message rather than a generic "too small".
2. Convert HEIC and strip non-sRGB colour profiles on the way in.
3. Offer a focal-point picker — a click on the image — and store the result
   alongside the file. It is one field and it removes most cropping complaints.
4. Store the original. Every derivative on the site is generated from it, so a
   later redesign that needs a bigger or differently-shaped version does not
   need the photographs taken again.
5. Strip GPS coordinates from EXIF. Photographs of a guide's home village
   should not publish its location.
